text:
Abstract
We quantified the proportion of Escherichia coli sequencing runs in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) whose study titles mention “carbapenem.” We used two ENA-derived endpoints: (1) BRC Analytics’ ENA proxy to obtain the total number of ENA runs for taxon 562 (E. coli), and (2) ENA’s portal search filtered to runs with tax_eq(562) and a study_title containing the substring “carbapenem.” The BRC endpoint reported 551,679 total E. coli runs. The ENA portal search reported 9,759 matching runs, with one example returned and the full count provided in metadata. The fraction was computed as 9,759 / 551,679 = 0.0177 (1.77%). This estimate depends on study-level title text rather than run-level annotations and may miss records that mention carbapenems elsewhere (e.g., sample titles or descriptions). The result provides a baseline measure of how often carbapenems are explicitly referenced in E. coli ENA study titles and can guide more targeted retrieval of carbapenem-related datasets for downstream antimicrobial resistance analyses.

I. Introduction
Background. Escherichia coli is a major human and animal pathogen. Carbapenems are critical last-resort antibiotics, and the emergence of carbapenem resistance in Enterobacteriaceae, including E. coli, is a global public health concern. Quantifying how frequently E. coli sequencing studies reference carbapenems helps scope available data for resistance-focused research.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. The proportion of E. coli ENA runs that explicitly reference carbapenems in their study titles was not established.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Estimate the fraction of E. coli ENA runs whose study titles mention “carbapenem.” Hypothesis: A small minority of E. coli runs will reference carbapenems in the study titles.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We combined an organism-level run count (all E. coli runs in ENA) with a text-filtered run count (E. coli runs in studies whose titles include “carbapenem”). The denominator was the total E. coli run count; the numerator was the count of E. coli runs matching the carbapenem title filter.
Materials.
- BRC Analytics ENA proxy (functions.brc_ena_runs) for total E. coli runs.
- ENA portal search (functions.brc_ena_search) for carbapenem title matches among E. coli runs.
Procedures.
- functions.brc_ena_runs with arguments: taxonomy_id="562", limit=1, offset=0. Purpose: obtain total_in_ena for E. coli.
- functions.brc_ena_search with arguments: taxonomy_id="562", title_contains="carbapenem", limit=1. Purpose: obtain total_matching runs with study titles containing “carbapenem.”
Statistical Analysis.
- Denominator: total_in_ena field from brc_ena_runs (551,679).
- Numerator: total_matching field from brc_ena_search (9,759).
- Fraction = numerator / denominator = 9,759 / 551,679 ≈ 0.0177. Percentage ≈ 1.77%.
- No deduplication was performed; counts are as reported by ENA endpoints.

III. Results
Data Presentation. Table 1.

| Metric                                    | Value   | Source field        |
|-------------------------------------------|---------|---------------------|
| Total E. coli runs in ENA                 | 551,679 | total_in_ena        |
| E. coli runs with “carbapenem” in title   | 9,759   | total_matching      |
| Fraction                                  | 0.0177  | computed (numer/den) |
| Percentage                                | 1.77%   | computed             |

Findings.
- The total number of ENA runs annotated to taxid 562 (E. coli) is 551,679.
- The number of E. coli runs whose study titles mention “carbapenem” is 9,759.
- The fraction is 0.0177, corresponding to 1.77%.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. Approximately 1.77% of E. coli ENA runs are in studies whose titles mention “carbapenem.” This supports the expectation that a minority of E. coli studies explicitly reference carbapenems in their titles.
Context. The numerator is constrained to study_title text matches, which identifies studies with explicit carbapenem focus or context. The denominator reflects all E. coli runs currently indexed in ENA.
Limitations.
- Title-based matching: “title_contains” searches study titles only, not sample/run titles or descriptions; carbapenem-related content not named in the title is not counted.
- Scope: The ENA search endpoint reported the total matching count while returning one example record; the count is authoritative, but only a single result is shown in the payload due to the limit parameter.
- Taxon scope: tax_eq(562) targets E. coli; this assumes ENA taxonomic annotation is correct for each run.
Conclusion & Future Directions. About 1.77% of E. coli ENA runs are associated with study titles mentioning “carbapenem.” Future work could broaden text fields (e.g., sample_title, run or study descriptions) or incorporate keyword variations (e.g., “carbapenemase”, specific drug names like “imipenem”, “meropenem”) to refine the estimate. We can also generate a downloadable table of the matching runs on request.

References
[1] BRC Analytics ENA proxy. https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/562
[2] ENA Portal Search (tax_eq(562) AND study_title="*carbapenem*"). https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search

Acknowledgments
We thank BRC Analytics for ENA-proxied run counts and the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) for study-level search and run metadata.
